order: The original Super Eagles selection for the Russia clash already contained several unfamiliar faces, but the squad has changed again.
With Ndidi gone from the squad, Michael has a clearer route to minutes and a chance to convince Chelle that his development can continue at international level.

His physical frame, youth and regular competitive football make him a serious long-term project, although Stanley Nwabali’s presence means a starting place on Tuesday is far from guaranteed. A convincing cameo could, however, put James into Chelle’s future goalkeeper rotation.

Chibuzo “Chibby” Nwoko arrives with one of the most unusual international stories in the squad. The 20-year-old London-born midfielder came through Chelsea before joining Fulham at Under-12 level and can operate as a six, eight or 10. His father has roots in Umuahia South, Abia State.

Wilfred Ndidi, Bright Osayi-Samuel and Victory Akpe have withdrawn, opening the door for teenage midfielder John Otomewo and 20-year-old centre-back Vince Osuji. The updated group therefore gives Chelle a collection of players whose international reputations are still being written, from Finnish goalkeeping prospect Samuel James to Benfica forward Peter Edokpolor and Kristiansund midfielder Igor Wilfred.

Chelle’s decision nevertheless offers a window into what the coach sees in him. Ajasa has spent more than a year developing inside Russian football, and his familiarity with the country’s footballing environment could prove useful against a Russian side Nigeria will face in its own territory.

Suleiman Mubarak is one of the youngest names in the squad at 19. The midfielder joined Slavia Prague in 2025 from Nigerian academy Rigt 2 Win after impressing during a trial that included training with the Czech club’s first team.
His ability to play on either flank also gives Chelle another attacking option after Bright Osayi-Samuel became the latest player to withdraw from the squad.
